explanation: Son of King David and his wife Maaka, who rebelled against his father and was killed in battle.
The second king of Israel, known for his skill as a warrior and musician, and the author of several psalms.
David's army commander and nephew, a loyal but also brutal warrior, who killed Absalom despite David's wish to spare him.
A man from Saul's tribe who mocked and cursed David when he fled from Absalom, but later asked for forgiveness.
An old and wealthy man from Gilead who helped David during his flight from Absalom and was rewarded for his loyalty.
Absalom's army commander and David's cousin, who was appointed by David as army commander after Joab's death, but was killed by Joab.
The name of the northern kingdom consisting of ten tribes, also used as a general name for the entire nation.
The name of the southern kingdom consisting of two tribes, also used as a general name for the entire nation.
